route._layer_rules_removed: REMOVED 8 Sep 2026 17:50: the per-class layer rule (rule 2) cost C8 three routes that never finished a pass (12 min, 90 min, 3 h with nothing written) while the same DSN without it auto-routed in 14 min 21 s; and the D9 read-back this morning showed the router does not hold a class to its layers anyway. route._ceiling_measured: 9 September 2026 19:05 CEST: this is the PROBE, not the release route. The rule of the record is that a pass ceiling comes from a measured 3-pass probe of THIS DSN, never from an ambition, and this DSN is not B18's: the I/O high-availability layer added 169 parts and 40 nets. Read the 3-pass rate off this run, then set the release ceiling from it in b19-release.json.
route._jar_unpinned: 11 September 2026: this pinned ~/bin/freerouting-1.9.0.jar, the STOCK jar, which set FR_JAR and so bypassed route_one's own choice AND its refusal. Our 1.9.0 build writes a session after every pass; the stock one writes one only when the whole job ends, so a run that is cut leaves nothing, which is what every NO_SESSION round in the record is. Unpinned: route_one takes the patched jar when the host has it and refuses when it does not, unless FR_REQUIRE_MESH=0 says otherwise deliberately.
route._attempts_why: 15 September 2026: this profile was the three-pass PROBE of 9 September, written to learn the pass rate of a board that was then held by the pair ruling. Under the coupled-fraction hold of decision 24 B routes for a deliverable, and the measured curve of its predecessor B16 is 3 passes 252 open, 5 passes 159, 12 passes 77, 16 passes 74, flattening near 70 (7 September). Twelve passes in six hours is the point on that curve the record can afford, and the rounds after it are the remedy table's.
